patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Demandbase and Ocean.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Demandbase and Ocean.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Demandbase only if your buying job matches “Enterprise ABM platform (Demandbase One) for account intelligence, intent, and go-to-marke” rather than Ocean.io's shape. Choose Ocean.io only if your buying job matches “Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichment — from ~$0.063/cr” rather than Demandbase's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Demandbase is shaped for Enterprise ABM platform (Demandbase One) for account intelligence, int whereas Ocean.io is shaped for Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichme. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Demandbase and Ocean.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Demandbase is Enterprise ABM platform (Demandbase One) for account intelligence, intent, and go-to-market orchestration — custom-quote packaging.; Ocean.io is Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichment — from ~$0.063/credit, ~$47/mo yearly headline..
- Company-size focus: Demandbase (mid-market, enterprise) vs Ocean.io (small-business, mid-market).
- Researched limits: Demandbase — Demandbase One pricing is custom quote only — no published seat list prices; Ocean.io — Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer.

Limitations — Demandbase: Demandbase One pricing is custom quote only — no published seat list prices; Enterprise ABM scope means substantial implementation and change-management cost; Ocean.io: Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer; Credit minimums and yearly packaging require modeling before comparing to seat tools.

Poor-fit cases: Demandbase is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Demandbase One pricing is custom quote only — no published seat list prices · Ocean.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer · Avoid Demandbase if you actually need Ocean.io's motion (Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichment — from )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
